caseno:
Death Reference No. 23 of 2006
Criminal Appeal No. 2245 and 4972, of 2006 and 2783, 2784 and 2785 of 2011
lawyer:
MA Mannan Mohon, Deputy Attorney-General with Mahabub-ul-Alam, Assistant Attorney General with Delowara Begum (Bela) Assistant Attorney General ------ For the State. 
AM Mohammad Azizul Haque ------ State Defence Lawyer (in Criminal Appeal No. 22450/2006) 
Abdul Halim Chaklader with Md Fakhar Uddin, Advocates ------ For the Appellant in Criminal Appeal No. 27850/2011. 
Khalifa Shamsum Nahar Bari, Advocate ------ For the Appellants in Jail Appeal Nos. 329 0/2006, 207 0/2006, 2080/2006 and 2090/ 2006. 
Anjuman Ara Begum, Advocate ------ For the Appellant in Jail Appeal No. 2100/2006.
parties:
State  ------ Appellant
Vs.
Delwar Hossain & 7 others  ------ Condemned Prisoners
full_judgment:
ANM Bashir Ullah, J: This Death Reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short, the Code) has been submitted by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Cox's Bazar for confirmation of sentence of death awarded by him upon the accused Nos. 1 to 8 convicting them under section 396 of the Penal Code by the judgment and Order dated 19-3-2006 passed in Session Case No. 12 of 2001. Criminal Appeal Nos. 2785 of 2011, 2783 of 2011, 2245 of 2006, 2784 of 2011, 4972 of 2006 and Jail Appeal Nos. 210 of 2006, 208 of 2006, 329 of 2006, 207 of 2006 and 209 of 2006 have been arisen out of the same judgment and Order of conviction and sentence. The death reference, criminal appeals and jail appeals have been heard together and are being disposed of by this common judgment. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that on 26-8-1996 at 9-00 AM PW 1 and informant Nurul Hossain along with 19 Japanese nationals and 7-8 local people were going to Cox's Bazar Sadar from Devdevi of Chokoria Police Station under Cox's Bazar district by a engine boat. At 9-30 AM when they reached at Mukbeki of Moheshkhali channel' near the Shaplapur Union, a speed boat having 8-9 dacoits tried to touch the boat of the informant party who were armed with gun and kata rifle. The dacoits rebuking the driver of the boat of the informant asked him to stop the boat but since he tried to leave the place of occurrence with speed the dacoits made gunshot targeting the driver Syed Ahmed and Syed Ahmed sustaining bullet injuries left the steering of the said boat. The dacoits tried to enter into the boat of the informant. The dacoits also made more gunshots causing bullet injuries to Saiful Islam Chowdhury and Nurul Bashar Bachhu, the accompanying members of the informant. At that stage of the occurrence ATM Nurul Islam Chowdhury, another member of the accompanying party of the informant in order to save their lives and property made gunshots causing bullet injuries at least on 2 dacoits. Noor Ahmed son of late Akbar Ahmed sustained bullet injuries as one of the dacoit. The informant party had identified dacoit Delowar Hossain. Since 2 dacoits sustained bullet injuries they left the place of occurrence. The informant in order to save the life of his accompanying injured members went to Shaplapur gate where they did not find any doctor. Thereafter, they moved to Badarkhali where Saiful Islam Choudhury succumbed to his injuries. The informant party came to know at Badarkhali that before launching attack on them to commit dacoity the same dacoits had committed dacoity with 2 engine boats also. The informant ultimately went to Malumghat Hospital from Badarkhali for the treatment of Syed Ahmed and Nurul Bashar Bachhu. The informant also came to know from there that the police of Chokoria had arrested one dacoit alive and another dead. He having been at Chokoria Police Station immediate after occurrence found the Officer-in-Charge of Moheshkhali Police Station who recorded the First Information Report (in short, the FIR) on the basis of his verbal narration and accordingly Moheshkhali Police Station Case No. 11 dated 26-8-1996 corresponding to GR No. 2612 of 1996 were started. The case was investigated by the Investing Officer who after completion of investigation submitted police report under sections 395/397/400/302 and 34 of the Penal Code recommending the trial of 8 accused named in the charge sheet and eventually the accused were put on trial before the Additional Sessions Judge, Cox's Bazar. The trial Court invited the accused-persons to make their answer on a charge framed under section 396 of the Penal Code. On the date of framing of charge accused Delowar Hossain, Giasuddin, Isahak, Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya were present before the Court who pleaded their not guilty and claimed to be tried. Since accused Helaluddin alias Pearu, Nur Alam alias Nurul Alam, Lalu and Shafique were absconding their answer on the charge could not be recorded. The absconding accuseds were duly defended by the State defence lawyer. 

 4. The defence case as it appears from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses is the case of innocence and false implication. The further defence taken is that the accused are innocent and they are not involved with the occurrence of this case. In fact, there appears no definite defence case on the part of the defence save and except the plea of innocence. 

 5. The learned Judge on consideration of the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case convicted and sentenced the accused as aforesaid and made the reference under section 374 of the Code for confirmation of the sentence of death awarded to the accused. Conversely accused Isahak Ali being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and Order of conviction and sentence preferred Criminal Appeal 2785 of 2011 and also Jail Appeal No. 210 of 2006, Giasuddin preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2783 of 2011 and Jail Appeal  No. 208 of 2006, Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2245 of 2006 and Jail Appeal No. 329 of 2006, Delowar Hossain preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2784 of 2011 and Jail Appeal No. 207 of 2006 and Nur Alam alias Nurul Alam preferred Criminal Appeal No. 4972 of 2006 and Jail Appeal No. 209 of 2006. 

 6. Mr AM Mannan Mohan, the learned Deputy Attorney General with Md Mahabub-ul- Alam and Mrs Delowara Begum (Bela), the learned Assistant Attorney Generals appearing on behalf of the State having taken us through the judgment and Order under the reference, the FIR, the charge sheet, the deposition of the prosecution witnesses, the confession of Delowar Hossain and other materials on record makes his submission supporting the reference and opposing the appeals. He submits that at the time of occurrence when the informant party along with some foreigners were going to Cox's Bazar from Devdevi of Chokoria Police Station by a boat and when they reached at Mukbeki of Moheshkhali channel the accused party stormed on them in order to commit dacoity but for the strong resistance made by the informant party they could not be successful. So, such action of the accused was a strong attempt to commit dacoity which amounts to commission of dacoity in view of section 391 of the Penal Code and at the time of occurrence the accused party made incriminating gunshot to the informant party in order to capture the boat and the persons present in the boat and also to take away the goods from them and for the gunshot of the accused party Saiful Islam Chowdhury met with his death and 2 other accompanying members of the informant sustained bullet injuries. Of course, one of the members of the informant party made counter gunshot targeting the dacoits which caused the death of dacoit Nur Hossain and for the said resistance the accused could not take away the booty from the foreigners and other accompanying members of the informant. The learned Deputy Attorney General also submits that the prosecution case has been proved by the evidence of ocular witnesses adduced by the prosecution at the time of trial inasmuch as by the confession of Delowar Hossain and the trial Court on due consideration of the evidence on record rightly found the accused guilty under section 396 of the Penal Code and the Court below rightly and legally awarded the conviction and death sentence to the accused. Thus, according to his submission there is no ground for interference in the judgment and Order of conviction and sentence and with these words he canvassed for acceptance of the reference and dismissal of the appeals filed by the convicts. 

 7. Mr Abdul Halim Chaklader, the learned Advocate with Md Fakhar Uddin appearing on behalf of the condemned-prisoner Isahak Ahmed make his submission opposing the reference and supporting the Criminal Appeal No. 2785 of 2011. He submits that from the very beginning of this case the Trial Court was misconceived in framing charge under section 396 of the Penal Code against the appellant and others as there was no ingredient of section 396 of the Penal Code in the occurrence of this case. He also adds that no dacoity was committed on the boat of the informant and no booty were taken away by the appellant and others. So the framing of charge under section 396 of the Penal Code was misnomer of law. 

 8. He next submits that the Trial Court relying on the confession of Delowar Hossain and evidence of PWs 2 and 4 found convict appellant lsahak guilty but the confessional statement of Delowar Hossain is not voluntary and true. He submits that Delowar Hossain was arrested immediate after occurrence on 26-8-1996 but in flagrant violation of the provisions of section 167 of the Code he was produced before the nearest Magistrate after 3 days of his arrest. So confession of such an accused who was detained illegally in the custody of police beyond the prescribed period of time cannot be considered as legal and fair. In support of his contention he referred the decision of the case of State vs Mofizuddin, reported in 24 BLD 481. He also submits that the confession of accused Delowar Hossain is not any substantive evidence against another co-accused lsahak. This type of confession can simply lend assurance to other independent evidence. But in this case there appears no such independent evidence against condemn prisoner appellant Isahak. 

 10. He next submits that in this case there are names of 40 witnesses in the police report out of which the prosecution could have examined only 10 witnesses and tendered 1 witness for cross-examination by the defence. The prosecution even did not examine the doctor to prove the death of victim Saiful Islam Chowdhury, The case was investigated by 4 Investigating Officers of which the prosecution has examined only one Investigating Officer, PW 11. So, the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the appellant is not sustainable in the eye of law. He further submits that there is a serious doubt as to the occurrence of the case as a whole and the Court below illegally convicted and sentenced the condemned-prisoner Isahak. Therefore, the impugned judgment and Order of conviction and sentence is not sustainable. Thus, he canvassed for rejection of reference and to allow the appeal acquitting condemned-prisoner Isahak. 

 11. Mr AM Mohammad Azizul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the condemned-prisoner Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya and also on behalf of the absconding convicts Lalu. Shafique and Helal Uddin submits that there is no independent evidence against the condemned-prisoner Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya and Lalu save and except the confessional statement of co-accused Delowar Hossain. But the confession of a co-accused cannot be the basis to find the guilt of another accused. Moreso, the confession of a co-accused is always weak type of evidence as the other accused did not get any chance to controvert the maker of confession and it is the settled principle of law that the confession of a Co-accused is not any substantive piece of evidence against another accused. But the Trial Court relying on the confession of co-accused of Delowar Hossain found Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya and Lalu guilty and awarded capital punishment on them. He next submits that at the time of occurrence there took place a free fight between the members of 2 boats at Moheshkhali channel. Saiful Islam Chowdhury, one of the victims of the boat of informant met with his death for the bullet injuries sustained at the time of occurrence. But at the same time and in the same occurrence Noor Mohammad also met with his death who was in another boat. But for such murder of Noor Mohammad no case was even filed although there should have been 2 cases for 2 separate murders in the same incident. He further submits that though in this case convicts Lalu, Shafique and Helal Uddin are fugitive from the very beginning of the case but mere abscondence of any particular accused does not mean that he was involved with the occurrence of the case. He further submits that PW 4 is the only witness who told the name of accused Helaluddin and Shafique but PW 4 was also one of the accompanying member of the informant in the boat at the time of occurrence but he did not state the name of the accused Helaluddin and Shafique to the informant that he could have identified those accused at the time of occurrence. So, the subsequent disclosure of the name of accused Helaluddin and Shafique by PW 4 at the time of trial is not believable. He next submits that there is no iota of evidence against accused Lalu. So, the trial Court without proper appreciation of the evidence on record found accused Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya, Lalu, Shafique and Helaluddin guilty under section 396 of the Penal Code. So, the reference as has been submitted by the trial Court to confirm their death sentence should be rejected. 

 12. Mrs Khallfa Sham sum Nahar Bari, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of condemned-prisoners Delowar Hossain, Giasuddin and Nur Alam submits that the Trial Court on the wrong assessment of the evidence on record found. Delowar Hossain, Giasuddin and Nur Alam guilty as there is no independent evidence against them. The confessional statements of accused Delowar Hossain is not voluntary and true inasmuch as before his such confession he was detained in police custody illegally. So, the reference submitted by the Trial Court should be rejected and the convicts should be acquitted from the case. 

 14. PW 1 Nurul Hossain, the informant of this case stated that on 26-8-1996 he along with 19 Japanese and also Saiful Islam Chowdhury, Mafidul Haque Manik, Nurul Bashar, Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Shamsul Islam, Ali Akbar and Chowdhury Syed Ahmed were going to Cox's Bazar from Devdevi of Chokoria Police Station by a boat and at 9.30 AM when they reached at Mukbeki of Moheshkhali channel near Shaplapur Union Parishad a boat having 8-9 persons armed with gun and kata rifle coming to them asked the driver to stop the boat, but when the boatman was trying to avoid the said command the dacoits made gunshot on the driver who sustaining bullet injuries failed to control the boat, they also tried to enter into their boat and at that stage they also made more gunshots causing bullet injuries to Saiful Islam and Nurul Bashar Bachhu. He further stated that Nurul Islam Chowdhury in return made two rounds gunshots to the dacoits from their boat and dacoit Nur Mohammad son of Akter Ahmed sustaining gunshot injuries met the death. He had identified accused Nur Mohammad and Delowar Hossain. He further stated that they went to Shaplapur for the treatment of injured persons but since there was no doctor at Shaplapur they had moved to Badarkhali where Saiful Islam succumbed to his injuries. They came to know that the dacoits before storming on them committed dacoity with boats. They also came to know that Chokoria Police had already arrested one of the dacoits alive and also held the dead body of another dacoit. He having been at Chokoria Police Station found the Officer-in-Charge of Moheshkhali Police Station to whom he narrated the occurrence recorded the First Information Report. PW 1 proved the FIR and his signature in it, marked as exhibits 1 and 1/1. He proved the inquest report of deceased Saiful Islam and his signature on it, marked as exhibits 2 and 2/1. In cross-examination he stated that Delowar did not tell the name of other accused in his presence. Saiful Islam Chowdhury met with his death on their boat. He denied the defence suggestion that he was not present in the boat and he did not witness the occurrence. 

 23. PW 11 and the last witness Md Mozahar Alam stated that he was posted at Mohesbkhali Police Station as Officer-in-Charge and he has investigated the present case but before his investigation Police Inspector Sagir Ahmed Talukder, Md Abdul Hamid and Serajuddin Talukder also had investigated the case. He perused the case diary, the map and index, visited the place of occurrence and he found similarity between the place of occurrence and the map and the index prepared earlier he did not repeat the same. He further stated that the map and index of the place of occurrence was prepared by the 1st Investigating Officer Serajuddin, marked as exhibits 7 and 8 respectively. He had seized two launches at his turn and gave the same in the jimma of others. He had examined the witnesses and recorded their statements and after completion of investigation submitted charge sheet under sections 395/397/400/302/34 of the Penal Code against the accused-persons. There was no cross-examination of PW 11 by the defence. 

 24. These are the evidences adduced by the prosecution in this case. 

 25. The learned Counsel on behalf of the condemned-prisoners and absconding convicts assailing the framing of charge under section 396 of the Penal Code submits that there was no ingredients of section 396 of the Penal Code in the occurrence of this case as no dacoity was taken place on the informant's boat and no goods were taken away by the accused. So the framing of charge under section 396 of the Penal Code against the condemned-prisoners as well as other convicts is unwarranted in law. In support of this contention, they referred the decision of the case of Md Abdul Ali vs State, reported in 20 BLD 327 = 6 BLC. 

 26. In the reported case this Court found that the witnesses could not prove the manner of occurrence, as such, it was held that in absence of any evidence of dacoity by any of the witnesses and in absence of any recovery of any article taken during the dacoity from the possession of any of the accused-person, it can safely be said that the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove the case of dacoity, therefore, the charge under section 396 of the Penal Code must fail. But the case in our hands to some extent different from that of the reported case. The case in our hands goes to show that the dacoits could not enter into the informant's boat and they could not also take away goods from the boat at the time of occurrence. They vigorously stormed on the informant's boat in order to commit dacoity i.e. they took serious attempt for committing dacoity. Generally dacoity means taking away of any goods forcibly from a person by 5 or more persons. But in order to appreciate the real meaning of dacoity we are to look into the definition of dacoity as has been defined in section 391 of the Penal Code. It would be profitable for all if we look into section 391 of the Penal Code, which runs as follows:- 

 30. In this regard the findings and decision of the case of Sirajuddin vs State, reported in AIR (38) 1951 Allahabad 834 is relevant for the present case. The question raised by the defence before us was also raised in the reported case which has been answered in the following ways: 

 So the word "dacoity" has been defined not only where a robbery is committed by five or more persons but where five or more persons had attempted to commit a robbery. In view of the definition of dacoity the argument that, as the dacoits were unsuccessful in removing any booty, no dacoity was committed, is misconceived." 

 33. He categorically submits that the doctor who held the post mortem examination on the dead body of Saiful Islam Chowdhury was not examined in this case. It is fact that the prosecution could not examine the doctor who held post mortem examination on the dead body of Saiful Islam nor there appears any explanation for the same. Medical evidence is a piece of corroborative evidence along with other evidence. If the prosecution case is proved by the ocular witness of the occurrence, the non-examination of the doctor is not always fatal. It depends upon as to how the other witnesses have been able to prove the occurrence of the case. PWs 1, 2, 3 and 4 testified that in their presence deceased Saiful Islam sustained bullet injuries from the dacoits in attempting to commit dacoity in their boat. PW 1 also testified that he rushed to Shaplapurghat for the treatment of Saiful Islam but since there was no doctor he moved to Badarkhali but before reaching to Badarkhali Saiful Islam succumbed to his injuries. He also went to Malumghat hospital where the doctor declared him dead. From the ocular evidence of PWs 1,2,3 and 4 it has been proved that Saiful Islam was done to death by the dacoits in attempting to commit dacoity. 

 34. We find support to the above contention from the case of State vs Ful Mia, reported in 5 ELC (AD) 41, wherein the Appellate Division held in the following ways:- 

 35. In the case of Keshab Chandra Mistry vs State, reported in 5 BLD (AD) 301, the Appellate Division also held on the subject in the following ways: 

 "It is true that in this case neither the post mortem report was produced nor doctor, who held post-mortem, was examined, but there are competent and natural witnesses, who proved the death of Bikash and who consistently stated that they saw marks of injuries on the dead body of Bikash. There is no reason to disbelieve their evidence." 

 36. The case in our hands shows that prosecution could not examine the doctor who held the postmortem no there appears any explanation for the same, but having regards to the decisions and the materials on record it appears that the murder of Saiful Islam has been proved by the evidence of PWs 1, 2, 3 and 4. So, the non-examination of the doctor who held the postmortem examination on the corpse of Saiful Islam is not fatal in this case. 

 37. PW, 1 testified that 8/9 dacoits stormed on them at the time of occurrence. PW 4 corroborating the evidence of PW 1 also testified that 8/9 dacoits stormed on them. There is nothing in the record to discard such evidence of PWs 1 and 4. So, it appears that an aggressive attempt of the accused comprising 8/9 dacoits in order to commit dacoity on the boat of informant and also in so attempting the murder of Saiful Islam have been proved by the ocular witnesses of the case which has ultimately fulfilled the ingredients of section 396 of the Penal Code. Thus the commission of offence punishable under section 396 of the Penal Code on 26-8-1996 at 9.30 AM at Mukbeki of Moheshkhali channel has been proved. Now, let us consider whether complicity of the accused in the commission of the said offence has been proved. 

 38. In this case there is a confession of accused Delowar Hossain. The learned Counsel for the condemned-prisoner submits that condemned-prisoner Delowar Hossain was arrested immediately after occurrence on 26-8-1996. Thereafter, without producing him within 24 hours as provided in sections 161 and 167 of the Code police produced him on 29-8-1996 before the Magistrate with a prayer for 5 days police remand which was allowed by the Magistrate and when he was in police remand for 5 days he was produced before the Magistrate (PW 10) for recording his confessional statements and accordingly he made a confessional statement before the PW 10. The learned Counsel submits that before recording his such confession he was illegally detained in the custody of police and that fact alone is sufficient to consider his confession as involuntary and untrue. The learned Counsel in support of his contention referred the case of State vs Mofizuddin, reported in 24 BLD 481 = 10 BLC 93. 

 39. It is fact that confessing accused Delowar Hossain was arrested on 26-8-1996 and he was produced for the first time before the Magistrate on 29- 8-1996 i.e. almost after 3 days of his arrest. But Delowar Hossain was not produced on 29-8-1996 before the Magistrate for recording his confessional statement rather he was produced before the Magistrate for 5 days remand which was ultimately allowed by the Magistrate. In the reported case of Mofizuddin it appears that Mofizuddin was arrested on 22-8-1997 at 12-00 PM and he was produced before the Magistrate on 24-8-1997 at 2-00 PM with a prayer for recording his confessional statement and ultimately his confessional statement was recorded and this Court held that since Mofizuddin was in police custody for more than 24 hours with- out obtaining any order of remand and without any explanation so his confession cannot be accepted as voluntary. With all regards to the decision of this Court in the case of Mofizuddin we are of the view that the arrest, production and confession of condemned-prisoner Delowar Hossain are quite distinguishable from that of the case of Mofizuddin. Had it been found that on 29-8-1996 Delowar Hossain was produced before the Magistrate with a prayer for recording his confessional statement surely we would find that the prolong custody of Delowar  "Hossain in violation of the provisions' of sections 161 and 167 of the Code renders his confession as in voluntary. When Delowar was produced for recording his confessional statement he was in the police remand and such police remand is lawful in the eye of law in view of section 167 of the Code. 

 40. Moreso, the confession of Mofizuddin did not tally with the facts and circumstances of that case and also with the other evidences on record. But in this particular case, the confessional statements of accused Delowar do tally with the facts, circumstances and other evidences on record. We do not appreciate the action of police detaining Delowar Hossain for 3 days in their custody beyond the prescribed time of law rather we seriously deprecate the police action in detaining Delowar in their custody for about two days without any lawful authority but since he was produced for recording confessional statement from the lawful police custody we cannot consider his such stay in the police custody as illegal and unfair. 

 41. Delowar Hossain in his confessional statement clearly stated that before storming on the informant's boat to commit dacoity they had also committed dacoity in 2 other boats and when they took a vigorous attempt to commit a dacoity on the informant's boat they sustained bullet injuries and when he and others were trying to provide treatment to their accomplice Nur Mohammad, the driver of a microbus with the help of others arrested him. The confessional statement of Delowar Hossain is fully consistent with the prosecution case as well as with the evidences on record. PWs 8 and 9 who were passengers of two separate boats at the relevant time of occurrence at Moheshkhali channel became subject matter of dacoity and they also stated that immediately after dacoity in their boats they had heard the sound of firing. The evidence of PWs 1,2, 3,4, 8 and 9 is consistent with the confessional statements of Delowar Hossain. 

 42. Moreso, PW 7 driver Jahangir Alam who carried accused Delowar and Nur Mohammad for treatment stated that whenever he could have guessed that accused Delowar is connected with the commission of an offence he with the help of others had nabbed Delowar. The evidence of PW 7 is also very much consistent with the confession of Delowar. So, we find no reason as to why the confession of Delowar will be thrown away on some technical ground. There appears full nexus between the confession of Delowar and the prosecution case. 

 43. In the reported case of 24 BLD 481 = 10 BLC 93 we find that Mofizuddin retracted his confession and at the time of examination under section 342 he made some allegations of torture which is very much absent in this case. Delowar made his confession on 5-9-1996 and the judgment of this case was pronounced almost after 10 years on 19-3-2006 but within this long 10 years condemned-prisoner Delowar did not retract his confession and at the time of examination under section 342 of the Code his attention was drawn in respect of his confession but he did-not raise his voice divulging any allegation of torture or inducement. The condemned-prisoner Delowar having got the repeated and prolonged chance to assail his confession did not raise any allegation. So at this stage any aspersion without any materials on such confession cannot be considered as genuine. 

 44. It is the settled principle of law that judicial confession if it is found to be true and voluntary, can indeed form the sole basis of conviction as against the maker of confession. This principle has been endorsed by the Appellate Division in the case of Islamuddin vs State, 13 BLC (AD) 81. We failed to discover any involuntary character of the confession of Delowar Hossain and untrue statements therein. The confessional statement of Delowar Hossain is harmonical with the prosecution case as well as with the evidence of other witnesses on record. He gave a true picture of the occurrence before the Magistrate involving himself with the occurrence. So, his confession appears to us voluntary and true. 

 45. Moreso, PW 1 in FIR clearly adverted that they could have identified accused Delowar Hossain at the time of occurrence. PW 1 testified that he had found accused Delowar Hossain at the time of occurrence. PWs 2, 3, and 4 corroborating the evidence of PW 1 testified that they could have identified accused Delowar at the time of occurrence. The evidence of PW s 1, 2, 3 and 4 in respect of identification and involvement of accused Delowar Hossain with the occurrence of this case appears to be believable and credible. These 4 witnesses were present in the boat at the time of occurrence and it is in the FIR also that the informant and others could have identified accused Delowar Hossain. There is nothing in the record for which the evidence of PW s 1, 2, 3 and 4 can be discarded in respect of Delowar Hossain. Thus the unblemished and unshaken evidence of PWs 1,2,3 and 4 that they found accused Delowar Hossain in the gang as one of the member of dacoits appears to be credible and the same is consistent with FIR also. So, if we consider the confessional statement of Delowar Hossain along with the evidence of PWs 1,2,3 and 4 there would have not better alternative but to find him guilty under section 396 of the Penal Code. 

 46. The trial Court found condemned-prisoners Nurul Alam alias Nurul Alam, Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya and the absconding convict Lalu relying on the confessional statement of Delowar Hossain. There appears no independent and substantive evidence against these 3 accused save and except the confessional statement of Delowar Hossain. Now it is settled principle of law that the confessional statement of an accused is not substantive piece of evidence against the one who did not confess and such evidence alone, without any substantive corroborative evidence cannot form the basis of conviction of co-accused. This principle of law has been endorsed by the Appellate Division in the case of Ustar Ali vs State, reported in 3 BLC (AD) 53. 

 47. In the case of Amir Hossain Howlader vs State, reported in 37 DLR (AD) 139 it was held, that the statement of a co-accused does not fall within the definition of evidence as given in section 3 of the Evidence Act. Section 30 of the Evidence Act, it simply makes the confession of a co-accused a relevant fact, in other words, the confessional statement of co-accused is admissible against other accused- persons in the sense that it may be taken into consideration against them along with other evidence. But it cannot be the sole basis of conviction of a co-accused. 

 48. In the case of Babor Ali Molla vs State, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 10 it was held that a confession made by co-accused in a joint trial for the same offence affecting himself and others may be taken into consideration and the confession of such an accused may lend assurance to other evidence on record. 

 51. The occurrence took place on 26-8-1996 at 9.30 AM and the FIR was lodged after 5-30 hours on the same day at 3-00 PM. Since PWs 2 and 4 were the accompanying members of the informant in the boat so it did not call for any explanation that if they would have seen accused Giasuddin and Isahak they must disclose or tell it to the informant and other persons precept in the boat and had it been so the name of these accused would have come in the FIR. PWs 2 and 4 had the opportunity to disclose the name of accused Giasuddin and Isahak at the eve of lodging FIR, but they without doing so disclosed their names for the first time at trial. There is no explanation from the prosecution as to non-closure of their names earlier. If there would have been a definite case that for any dreadful situation the eye witnesses could not state the name of the accused immediate after occurrence in that case only reliance can be placed on such belated disclosure of the name of any accused. But there appears no such explanation from the side of prosecution. 

 52. In this regard we can also rely on some decisions of our jurisdiction. The Appellate Division in the case of Nowabul Alam vs State, reported in 15 BLD (AD) 54= 45 DLR (AD) 140 held in the following ways:- 

 "When eye-witnesses witness the occurrence, accused-persons depart from the scene and nearly 1,000 people assemble at the place of occurrence followed by high officials, it is expected that the eye-witnesses will name the accused-persons not only to their own kith and kin but also to uninvolved persons including the high officials. Both the trial Court and the High Court Division failed to scrutinize the evidence of PWs 3-5 in so far as the disclosure of the names of the accused-persons to assembled persons are concerned, especially when the defence case is that after making a GD Entry stating that some miscreants had committed the murder, the accused-persons, the sworn enemies of the informant party, were roped in as an afterthought and careful planning by PW 1" (para 28 of the judgment). 

 53. In the above reported case the PWs 3-5 deposed before the trial Court as eye witnesses and disclosed the names of some accused which they did not disclose earlier, the Appellate Division considered there such evidence as afterthought. 

 54. This Court in the case of Nizamuddin vs State, reported in 11 BLC 688 observed in the following ways: "Furthermore, when an eye-witness to the occurrence that took place at night does not disclose the names of the assailants, the alleged recognition, the means of recognition and other material facts to the witnesses who came to the scene immediately after the occurrence or at the earliest opportunity and there is no justifiable reason for non-disclosure of the material facts, belated disclosure of material facts renders his testimony doubtful. In such a case the Court should reasonably infer that the story of recognition of the assailants was a subsequent embellishment" (para 26 of the judgment). 

 55. From the reported case it appears that the eye-witness of the occurrence did not state that he witnessed the occurrence at the earliest opportunity and the witness also did not state the said facts to others who came to them immediate after occurrence although he without any explanation of such non-disclosure of fact deposed in the trial Court as eye witness. This Division did not rely on the evidence of such type of eye-witness. We find it difficult to make any difference between the eye-witnesses of the reported case and the witness of the case in our hands.

 57. Since the eye-witness claimed to have recognized some accused at the time of occurrence but their names were not mentioned in the FIR and ultimately this Court disbelieved the evidence of such witness. The similar view was also taken in the case of Abdul Hakim alias Henju vs State, reported in 8 BLC 362. 

 58. The case in our hands goes to show that PWs 2 and 4 as spot witnesses claimed to have seen Giasuddin and Isahak but their names were not mentioned in the FIR PWs 2 and 4 as spot witnesses for the first time disclosed the name of condemned prisoner Giasuddin and Isahak at the time of trial before the Court below although they had opportunity to disclose the same before lodging FIR. Whenever any occurrence or murder is witnessed by the witnesses of a gathering what may be the probable and natural follow up of those eye-witnesses. In our consider ration excepting in some exceptional circumstances those witnesses will share the culpability of the accused disclosing their names among themselves and others including the kith and kin of the victims to bring the accused into the book of police so that accused cannot be gone unpunished. But the eye-witnesses of instant case did not disclose the names of accused at earliest opportunity without having any explanation for the same. As such, the non-disclosure of the names of the accused at the earliest opportunity and also the belated disclosure of their names by PWs 2 and 4 renders their evidence as unreliable, unbelievable and incompatible in the fact and circumstances of the case. It is a matter of common sense and gumption that the informant and the men of his cluster will try to name the accused in the FIR ardently and assiduously which they could have recognized at the time of occurrence. 

 59. So, we are of the firm opinion that had the accused Giasuddin and Isahak been seen by PWs 2 and 4 they would have told their names to the informant at the eve of lodging FIR. So, we find no minimum reason to believe the evidence of PWs 2 and 4 in respect of involvement of accused Giasuddin and Isahak with the occurrence of this case. So, the evidence before the Trial Court that PW s 2 and 4 found accused Giasuddin and Isahak in the boat of the dacoity cannot be considered as legal, fair and credible evidence at all. 

 62. Now, in sum up of the case we find that the conviction and sentence awarded upon condemned- prisoner Delowar Hossain is based on his self-confession which appears to be voluntary and true. Apart from the said confession of confessing accused Delowar Hossain PWs 1, 2, 3 and 4 also have proved the involvement and presence of Delowar Hossain with the gang of dacoits in the commission of offence under section 396 of the Penal Code by their cogent and reliable testimony. 

 67. Let the condemned-prisoners Giasuddin, Isahak, Kamal Hossain alias Gundiya, Nur Alam alias Nurul Alam be set free from the custody if not wanted in connection with any other cases. Let the process if issued against absconding convicts Helaluddin alias Pearu, Lalu and Shafique be called for.
